% Self-adjointness (time-reversibility) of an integrator
\begin{equation}\label{eq:A14-self-adjoint-def}
L(\Delta t)\,L(-\Delta t) \;=\; I \qquad \text{for all } \Delta t
\end{equation}

% Strang splitting is self-adjoint
\begin{equation}\label{eq:A14-Strang-self-adjoint}
\bigl[e^{(\Delta t/2)\,\mathcal{X}}\,e^{\Delta t\,\mathcal{Y}}\,e^{(\Delta t/2)\,\mathcal{X}}\bigr] \cdot \bigl[e^{(-\Delta t/2)\,\mathcal{X}}\,e^{-\Delta t\,\mathcal{Y}}\,e^{(-\Delta t/2)\,\mathcal{X}}\bigr] \;=\; I
\end{equation}

% Lie splitting is NOT self-adjoint
\begin{equation}\label{eq:A14-Lie-not-self-adjoint}
\bigl[e^{\Delta t\,\mathcal{Y}}\,e^{\Delta t\,\mathcal{X}}\bigr] \cdot \bigl[e^{-\Delta t\,\mathcal{Y}}\,e^{-\Delta t\,\mathcal{X}}\bigr] \;=\; I - \Delta t^{2}\,[\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}] + O(\Delta t^{3})
\end{equation}

% Consequence: self-adjoint integrators are even-order
\begin{equation}\label{eq:A14-even-order}
\text{Self-adjointness implies the leading error is at an EVEN power of } \Delta t; \text{Strang is 2nd order, not 1st.}
\end{equation}

% Kernel realisation (both forms equivalent)
\begin{equation}\label{eq:A14-kernel-chain}
\mathcal{X}(\Delta t/2)\,\mathcal{Y}(\Delta t/2)\,\mathcal{Y}(\Delta t/2)\,\mathcal{X}(\Delta t/2) \;\equiv\; \mathcal{X}(\Delta t/2)\,\mathcal{Y}(\Delta t)\,\mathcal{X}(\Delta t/2) \qquad \text{(§A13 kernel-chain equivalence)}
\end{equation}
